ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Primary AML/CFT legislation comprises the Money Laundering Control Act, the Counter-Terrorism Financing Act, the Regulations Governing Anti-Money Laundering of Financial Institutions, and the Regulations Governing Anti-Money Laundering of Businesses Required to Conduct Customer Due Diligence. Beneficial ownership reporting is principally governed by Article 22-1 of the Company Act and the Regulations Governing Company Registration and Information Reporting under Article 22-1. Mainland Chinese investment is subject to the Act Governing Relations between the People of the Taiwan Area and the Mainland Area, its Enforcement Rules, and Measures Governing Investment Permits to the People of the Mainland Area.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation, screen all shareholders, directors, supervisors, responsible persons, authorized signatories, intermediaries, lenders, licensors, licensees, and identified beneficial owners against United Nations Security Council sanctions, Taiwan domestic sanctions and designated-terrorist lists, OFAC lists, applicable European Union and United Kingdom lists, and relevant export-control and proliferation-financing lists. Apply enhanced due diligence to politically exposed persons, their family members, and known close associates; document source of wealth, source of funds, control rights, adverse media, sanctions rationale, and escalation decisions. Do not treat an OFAC designation as automatically binding Taiwan law, but treat it as a material banking, correspondent-bank, export-control, and reputational risk. Obtain senior-management approval before onboarding a PEP or high-risk counterparty and conduct ongoing transaction monitoring of royalty, intercompany, and SWIFT payments.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce, Company, Business and Limited Partnership One-stop Service; official portal: https://onestop.nat.gov.tw/
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must comply with the Company Act, Article 18, and the Name and Business Scope Pre-Check Review Standards. The name must be distinguishable from existing registered names and must not mislead the public as to business type, governmental status, or regulated activity. Chinese-language registration is the operative registration format. An English name may be used for commercial and banking purposes but does not replace the statutory Chinese name. Foreign investor names and business descriptions must be translated or transliterated consistently in the application. Business activities must be stated using the applicable Taiwan business-code classification and may not imply an unlicensed financial, securities, insurance, trust, banking, telecommunications, education, or governmental function.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: words implying a regulated financial, insurance, educational, medical, governmental, or public-utility function
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: File the company-name and business-scope pre-check application electronically through the Ministry of Economic Affairs one-stop portal or with the competent local registration authority. If rejected, obtain the written or electronic rejection reason, compare the proposed name against the Company Act and applicable review standards, and amend the name or business scope. A procedural challenge may be submitted to the issuing authority with supporting evidence of distinctiveness and lawful business activity; a formal administrative appeal may then be filed under the Administrative Appeal Act within the statutory appeal period stated in the decision, ordinarily thirty days from service. The appeal should include the rejection decision, applicant identity, legal grounds, evidence of non-confusion, and any revised name. Do not use the rejected name in contracts, invoices, banking applications, or public marketing pending approval. A pre-check approval generally remains usable for six months; verify the current validity and extension rules at filing because the approval period is not a universal thirty-day reservation period.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A registered office address is mandatory. A virtual office may be accepted for a non-regulated intellectual-property holding and licensing company if the address is legally usable for company registration, the landlord or service provider consents, mail and official notices can be received, and the company can demonstrate actual management, accounting, contract administration, royalty-control, and record-retention arrangements. A virtual office is unsuitable where the company conducts manufacturing, warehousing, laboratory, customer-facing operations, regulated financial activity, or activities requiring premises inspection. For a Mainland China-linked investor, a virtual office does not remove investment-permit, beneficial-owner, tax-substance, transfer-pricing, foreign-exchange, or banking scrutiny.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium. No reliable public statistical rate exists. For a pure IP holding and cross-border licensing company with a compliant registered address, the indicative operational risk of an unannounced or documentary-triggered address inspection during the first twenty-four months is approximately 10%–25%, increasing materially if the address is a mass-registration site, mail is undeliverable, tax filings are inactive, royalty flows are unusually large, beneficial ownership is opaque, or the investor is Mainland China-linked. Maintain lease or occupancy evidence, signage where required, accounting records, board minutes, licensing agreements, transfer-pricing support, bank records, and reachable personnel.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act, Articles 128–153 (company limited by shares and equity structure), Article 172 (board meetings), Article 387 (registration), Supplementary Rules on Company Registration; Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals, Articles 7–10; Regulations on Investment in Taiwan by Mainland Area Investors (as applicable).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan; One-Stop Company Registration Service for foreign-invested companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation and Company Registration Application Form (公司設立登記申請書及公司章程)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital; however, the Joint Venture must remit committed capital (recommended US$100,000 equivalent) into a Taiwan bank escrow account opened in the Company's intended name, obtain a bank deposit certificate, and attach that certificate to the registration filing.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) that the subscription of the Company's shares by each founder as set forth in the subscriber ledger is hereby accepted; (2) that the registered office of the Company is fixed at Suite 12, 15F, No. 7, Sec. 5, Xinyi Rd., Taipei City, Taiwan, and the Company may lease additional administrative offices; (3) that [Name A] be and is hereby appointed Chairperson, [Name B] General Manager, and [Name C] Corporate Secretary, each to serve until successors are duly elected; (4) that the officers are authorized to execute the Taiwan Company Act registration, open bank accounts, and sign all contracts necessary to carry into effect these resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment and Joint Venture Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (Taiwan)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the online investment application through the MOEA Investment Commission e-Government portal. Submit the Joint Venture agreement, investor identity documents, IP contribution valuation report, and capital adequacy statement. Pay the review fee and await approval letter before proceeding to company registration.
required_dossiers: Certificate of corporate existence or investor passport/domicile proof
Audited financial statements or bank reference from each investor
Valuation report of intellectual property contributed as capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to any supplemental inquiry within 30 days; revise the business plan or capital contribution structure and resubmit. If the Investment Commission rejects the application, file an administrative appeal through MOEA within 30 days of the rejection notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commerce, MOEA – Company Name Reservation System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to three Chinese and English company names using the online Name Reservation service. The name must not be identical to or confusingly similar to any existing Taiwan registered company. The reservation is valid for six months.
required_dossiers: Applicant's national ID or passport copy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected, submit an alternative name through the same portal; no penalty is imposed, and the reservation request may be amended online free of charge.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Escrow Deposit and Constitutional Documents Execution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan commercial bank acting as escrow agent; corporate legal counsel / certified public accountant
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary escrow account in the Company's intended name, remit the paid-in capital, and obtain a bank capital deposit certificate. Concurrently, founders must sign the Articles of Incorporation and hold an organizational meeting to approve the first board members and statutory representative.
required_dossiers: Bank remittance receipt for paid-in capital
Articles of Incorporation signed by all founders
Appointment forms for directors, supervisor, and chairperson
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the escrow account due to name mismatch, rectify the name with the MOEA name reservation and reopen the account. If the Articles of Incorporation are returned for inconsistency, amend by unanimous founder consent and re-notarize where required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Registration with the Department of Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commerce, MOEA – One-Stop Company Registration Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Company Registration Application and all supporting attachments through the Online Company Registration Portal. Pay the statutory registration fee. After approval, the Company receives its Certificate of Incorporation and registration serial number; obtain the official company seal at the local MOEA office if applicable.
required_dossiers: Directors' and supervisors' consent to appointment
Registered office proof (lease agreement or title deed)
ID copies of directors, supervisor, and chairperson
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Department issues a deficiency notice, correct the defects and resubmit within 15 days. If electronic signatures are invalid, convert to a physical filing at the MOEA regional office with original seals and supporting documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Tax Registration and Uniform Invoice Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance (local district office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, file the Tax Registration Application to obtain a Business Tax Registration Number (Tax ID). Register for uniform invoice forms. If the company will charge royalties to non-Taiwanese residents, apply for zero-percent VAT treatment or exemption on cross-border royalty income as relevant under the VAT Act.
required_dossiers: Registered office lease or ownership certificate
Tax ID application form signed by statutory representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For missing documentation, provide the required items in person during the tax bureau working hours. If the zero-VAT application is denied, file a written administrative appeal to the National Taxation Bureau and, if necessary, the Ministry of Finance within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Compliance and Bank Account Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company registry; local labor and social insurance office; commercial bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Activate the permanent corporate bank account, issue share certificates, and maintain the statutory books (shareholders' register, board minutes, and meeting records). Register as a labor insurance and pension unit if hiring employees. Complete any local government business license filings required for the office location.
required_dossiers: Resolution authorizing permanent bank account opening
Office lease and building usage permit for administrative use
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires director physical verification, arrange a personal visit by the appointed director. If labor insurance registration is overdue, pay any administrative fine and submit a late registration request; corporate registration defects may be cured by filing amended minutes with the MOEA.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – the entity is an intellectual property holding and licensing company with no manufacturing or physical plant.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable – no operating license is required for ISIC 6420 activities under Taiwan's industrial licensing regulations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – office-based IP licensing activities have no project scope requiring an EIA under Article 4 of the Environmental Impact Assessment Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable – no wastewater, VOC, or hazardous waste discharges are generated. If future tenants' facilities include emergency generators, comply with Taiwan Air Pollution Control Act emissions standards and local stationary source permit requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable for IP licensing. However, the leased office must maintain valid building structural load certificates, fire safety inspection reports, and workplace safety clearance from the local fire department and labor inspection authority to protect employees and visitors.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance, Taxation Agency, Taiwan (財政部賦稅署); principal operating contact is the local National Taxation Bureau of the seat of incorporation. Primary portals: MOF Tax Administration Portal (https://www.etax.nat.gov.tw) and E-Invoice Integration Platform (https://www.einvoice.nat.gov.tw).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a newly incorporated Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture: (1) complete company/branch registration with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and obtain the company registration number and corporate identification code; (2) within 15 days after incorporation, file for tax registration at the competent National Taxation Bureau pursuant to Article 28 of the Business Tax Act; (3) receive the Unified Business Number (統一編號) and, if taxable, the VAT/Business Tax registration certificate; (4) where electronic invoices will be issued, register for the E-Invoice Integration Platform and obtain a Turnkey/API credential; (5) if goods are to be exported, register separately with Customs as an exporter/importer; (6) if paying foreign royalties or non-resident service fees, register as a withholding taxpayer and obtain the relevant withholding rate approvals.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; resident Taiwan-incorporated JV is taxed on worldwide profit-seeking income under the Income Tax Act, at 20% corporate income tax, plus a 5% surtax on undistributed retained earnings; the JV is not a pass-through vehicle. A branch of a foreign entity remains separately classified as a non-resident branch, subject to 20% income tax plus 15% branch-profits remittance tax if profits are remitted out of Taiwan, unless reduced by a tax treaty.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Taiwan does not provide a US-style check-the-box election; tax classification follows legal entity form under the Company Act. Relevant elections include: financial-holding-company consolidated filing (only for qualified financial holding groups); election to use functional currency for tax accounts; election to calculate export zero-rated VAT refund without physical retail invoices; election to use the simplified 1% rate applicable to small-scale business taxpayers (only if monthly sales remain below the threshold); and formal Advance Pricing Agreement with the tax authority for cross-border royalty flows. Hybrid mismatch elections are not generally recognized; Taiwan has not adopted comprehensive hybrid mismatch legislation, but anti-avoidance principles under Article 43-1 of the Income Tax Act and the Corporate Income Tax Anti-Tax Avoidance Rules may recharacterize abusive royalty arrangements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taiwan Business Tax, 加值型及非加值型營業稅)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For a licensed corporate entity, business tax registration is mandatory before business commencement. Small-scale business operators with monthly taxable sales below NT$80,000 for goods or NT$40,000 for services may apply for registration exemption; foreign cross-border electronic service suppliers must register for simplified business tax when annual Taiwan-sourced digital services revenue exceeds NT$480,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan mandates the issuance of Uniform Invoices (統一發票) by all VAT-registered business entities. Large and designated business entities must issue cloud e-invoices through the Ministry of Finance E-Invoice Integration Platform, with approved software or Turnkey API transmission to the fiscal authority. There is no general real-time fiscal-stamp requirement for each invoice, but electronic invoices must be transmitted to the platform within the prescribed filing cycle, and every Business Tax return must be filed every two months along with the summary uniform-invoice data. Export zero-rated sales must be reported separately and substantiated on the return; failure to file accurately triggers penalty review.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under Article 7 of the Business Tax Act for: (i) exports of goods accompanied by customs outward declarations; (ii) domestic services or intellectual-property licenses provided to, or used by, foreign enterprises or individuals outside Taiwan, including royalty income under a patent/trademark sub-licensing arrangement where the licensed IP is exploited abroad; and (iii) services in connection with exported goods. For the IP HoldCo, the licence agreement must demonstrate that the licensee is a foreign entity, the licensed territory and use are outside Taiwan, and the consideration is received in foreign currency; the VAT on input purchases attributable to the zero-rated export services is then creditable or refundable.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Uniform Invoice issued as an export zero-rated invoice (外銷零稅率發票/中英文OPT invoice)
Patent/trademark licence agreement and sub-licence chain evidencing foreign beneficial use and territory
Foreign exchange receipt or inward remittance certificate (央行外匯水單/賣匯證明) evidencing collection of royalty proceeds
Customs export declaration (出口報單) and bill of lading / airway bill — required only where patented goods, prototypes, or media are physically exported
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Taxation Bureau cross-checks zero-rating claims against customs export data, banking foreign-exchange settlement records, and e-invoice filing data. If an export is recharacterized as a domestic taxable supply, the 5% VAT is assessed retrospectively with interest, and under Article 51 of the Business Tax Act, a penalty of 1 to 5 times the evaded tax may be imposed. Fabricating customs declarations, remittance certificates, or licence agreements triggers criminal liability under the Tax Evasion Punishment Act, and for deliberate evasion the statutory assessment period is 7 years; immediate VAT refunds are clawed back with interest before any penalty decision.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) under the People's Bank of China (PBOC); for the Taiwan counterparty, the central monetary authority of Taiwan (Central Bank of China, Taiwan, 'CBC') and the Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The RMB is convertible for genuine current-account service transactions, including IP licensing royalties, but all conversions must pass through a designated foreign-exchange bank's authenticity and legality review. Capital-account items, such as the initial FDI equity injection, intercompany loans and post-investment liquidation proceeds, remain subject to SAFE registration or approval and cannot be freely swapped or settled without the required regulatory evidence. Profit remittance by the JV to the Taiwan shareholder is operationally treated as a current-account 'investment income' payment but carries meaningful hurdles: the JV must complete enterprise income tax final settlement, present audited statutory financial statements showing accumulated distributable profits, pass a board resolution for the profit distribution, and provide a valid Taiwan tax-residency certificate if treaty/tax-agreement relief is claimed; absent that certificate a 10% dividend withholding tax will apply. Onshore TWD/CNY conversion has no liquid direct market, so cross-currency flows are normally settled through USD or via offshore CNH/TWD platforms at the Taiwan treasury level.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory export-receipt surrender obligation or mandatory conversion ratio in China. The JV may retain 100% of export and service-trade proceeds in foreign currency in its domestic current-account FX account, or convert them into RMB onshore at market rates. All receipts must nevertheless be repatriated through an SAFE-licensed bank and declared in the Balance of Payments / trade monitoring system. Receipts classified as trade-in-goods collections must be received within the contractual trade term; advance receipts and abnormally deferred receipts must be flagged in the SAFE digital monitoring platform to avoid becoming a 'focus verification enterprise'. For IP licensing royalties, export verification is replaced by concurrent documentary matching of agreements, invoices, tax filings and beneficial-ownership evidence at the bank; no fixed percentage of incoming FX must be converted into RMB.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Company Data Report (Company Act Article 20-1; MOEA Company Annual Report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 30 June for data as at the preceding 31 December; online filing opens 1 March.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: MOEA rectification order; administrative fine of TWD 10,000–500,000; repeated non-filing after final notice can lead to administrative strike-off of the company registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually 1 May – 31 May for calendar-year taxpayers; accountant-prepared filings may be extended to 30 June.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 3% of underpaid tax per month (capped at 15%); monthly interest on late payment; enforced collection and distraint for prolonged non-payment; no direct administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting and Adoption of Financial Statements and Business Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company shareholders; minutes kept at registered office; director/supervisor changes filed with MOEA within 15 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of fiscal year-end, i.e., by 30 June for calendar-year companies.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Shareholders may apply to MOEA for an extraordinary convocation if the meeting is not duly convened; directors may be liable under Company Act Articles 170 and 173; failure to file resulting director changes may attract fines.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Article 22-1 Register Update for Directors, Supervisors, Managers and 10%+ Shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs Company Registration Information System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Event-driven within 15 days of each relevant change; annual reconciliation must be completed by the 30 June Annual Data Report deadline.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of TWD 50,000–500,000 for non-disclosure or false declaration, plus continued periodic fines until corrected; no automatic strike-off for isolated event-driven lapses.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory CPA-audited financial statements are required for public companies, financial/securities institutions, and companies whose paid-in capital reaches NT$30 million or more under Company Act Article 20 and Financial Supervisory Commission regulations. Non-public companies below the threshold may produce unaudited statements unless the tax authority requires an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Non-public enterprises apply Taiwan Enterprise Accounting Standards (TEAS) / ROC GAAP under the Business Entity Accounting Act; public companies and financial institutions apply IFRS as endorsed by the Financial Supervisory Commission.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Taiwan does not maintain a standalone annual UBO certificate. Under Company Act Article 22-1, transfer of shares causing any person to hold 10% or more, and all changes in directors/supervisors/managers, must be entered in statutory registers and reported to MOEA within 15 days. The annual Company Data Report filed by 30 June constitutes the annual confirmation of ownership and beneficial-control data; registered shareholders are responsible for correcting shareholding information before the filing deadline.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 450 – USD 1,500 per year for registered office/agent services in Taiwan
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 – USD 8,500 per year where a CPA audit is mandatory or required by the foreign-investment approval; not required below the NT$30 million threshold

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No patent-box or IP-specific statutory tax holiday. A 5% retained-earnings surtax on undistributed profits applies under ITA Art. 66-9. The Alternative Minimum Tax rate is 12%. R&D and talent-training investment tax credits may reduce the effective rate, subject to a 50% cap on tax payable and 4-year credit limitation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return (Form 10), submitted electronically through the Ministry of Finance Tax E-Portal (e-Tax; https://www.etax.nat.gov.tw). Quarterly provisional tax returns are filed on Form 10-T.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Fifth month following the fiscal year-end, i.e., 31 May for calendar-year taxpayers; a one-month extension to 30 June applies where the return is certified by a licensed CPA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification: unified business number, company name, registered address, board composition and fiscal year-end.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Taiwan resident JV is the filing taxpayer; enter Taiwan registry details. If central management and control are treated as being in Taiwan under the PEM rule, the JV must file as a resident and cannot elect branch treatment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross operating revenue: royalty and licensing fees, intercompany service fees, and proceeds from IP sales.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the full amount of Taiwan-source licensing income on a gross basis; attach arm's-length documentation and any applicable treaty credits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-business income: interest, dividends, foreign-exchange gains and financial asset disposal gains.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Segregate foreign-source income for excess credit limitation; Taiwan-source income remains fully taxable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses: patent amortization, legal fees, intercompany management fees, and royalties paid to related parties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany royalties are deductible only if supported by economic substance and an arm's-length pricing study; attach TP schedules and WHT certificates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax-exempt income, special deductions and investment tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No participation exemption for foreign-source income unless underlying taxes were paid; DTA credits apply only where a treaty is effective.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax payable before credits, plus the retained earnings surtax on undistributed surplus.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Distributed dividends to a non-resident shareholder trigger 20% WHT; undeclared surplus triggers the 5% surtax at the entity level.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a 3% monthly surcharge on the tax due, capped at 30%; late payment interest accrues at the Postal Savings Bank rate plus 1% per month; underpayment due to misstatement is penalized up to twice the short-paid tax; intentional evasion is prosecuted criminally.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% for dividends distributed to a non-resident enterprise shareholder; 21% for a non-resident individual shareholder.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident claimant must deliver to the Taiwan payer, before each payment, a certificate of tax residence from the DTA counterparty, Form 104 (Withholding-Rate Reduction Application) and an updated beneficial ownership statement. The payer files with the National Taxation Bureau and retains the approved certificate. No Taiwan-PRC DTA is in force; therefore, a mainland China parent receives the statutory 20% WHT and may claim a foreign tax credit in mainland China for the Taiwan tax borne.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties and license fees: statutory WHT 20%; interest: statutory WHT 20%. Under Taiwan DTAs with e.g., Japan, Korea, Germany, rates may be reduced to 10% for royalties and 10% for interest where the recipient is the beneficial owner. A mainland China payee cannot invoke DTA reduction due to absence of a DTA.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: NT$100 million aggregate related-party transactions in one tax year triggers a full Local File; NT$500 million aggregate controlled transactions additionally requires a Master File. A simplified Local File is accepted when total controlled transactions are between NT$50 million and NT$100 million. CbC reports are required for MNE groups with consolidated revenue exceeding NT$270 billion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Taiwan does not apply OECD-style Economic Substance Regulations, but its GAAR, CFC and PEM rules impose a substance-over-form test. A Taiwan IP licensing holding company must have real employees, a physical office, independent board authority, complete books, and active IP management functions; otherwise the tax authority may disregard the entity, deny the royalty deduction, and attribute income to the ultimate principals.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional underreporting of Taiwan-source royalty/licensing income; falsification of books and records; issuance of false invoices for licensing services; maintaining dual accounting systems.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of the short-paid tax of one to three times under ITA Art. 110; criminal liability under Tax Collection Act Art. 41 with imprisonment up to five years and fines up to NT$1,000,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or direct the false return are jointly and severally liable for the deficiency, subject to civil restitution, asset attachment, travel bans and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying royalties or license fees to a related foreign vehicle without functional and economic substance; failing to prepare or file contemporaneous TP documentation; adopting non-arm's-length prices; circular or conduit license arrangements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reallocation of income under ITA Art. 43-1; denial of the royalty deduction; statutory 20% WHT on the disallowed payment; penalty of up to twice the additional tax; criminal prosecution where deliberate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly authorize the sham pricing can be personally liable for the additional tax and penalties, subject to civil suit and travel bans.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a Taiwanese JV with no physical office, employees, board meetings, or independent decision-making in Taiwan for the patent licensing business; routing royalty income through the entity and distributing it abroad without local substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disregard of the entity; denial of intra-group deductions; 20% withholding tax on deemed dividends; registration revocation under the Company Act; cumulative late-filing and underpayment penalties up to 30% plus twice the tax, as applicable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director may be personally liable for unpaid taxes and penalties when the corporate veil is pierced; civil restitution and a prohibition on holding future directorships may apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to register ultimate beneficial owners; failure to file suspicious transaction reports for abnormal cross-border royalty payments; failure to conduct customer due diligence on parent/licensee; use of shell bank accounts in tax havens.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Money Laundering Control Act, fines up to NT$6,000,000, revocation of business registration, and criminal imprisonment of up to seven years for willful laundering.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers are personally liable for willful omission; personal fines, imprisonment, travel bans and freezing of corporate bank accounts may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends or paying royalties to a mainland Chinese parent without withholding 20%; falsely invoking a DTA exemption without a next treaty or tax residency certificate; masking profit distribution as tax-free intercompany loans.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The payer is liable for the un-withheld tax plus an equal penalty, a 3% monthly late-filing surcharge capped at 30%, and daily interest from the payment date.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorize the unlawful remittance are jointly liable for the uncollected withholding, may be subject to travel bans, and face criminal prosecution for deliberate non-collection.
